description: Consolidate code review into a SINGLE review gate that validates the WHOLE pipeline (CI green) AND the PR comments (resolved), not just the diff; always posts the COMPLETE result to BOTH the PR and the responsible issue (what was done + link + full info); and only unlocks the approve/merge path (applies crewflow:reviewed enabling merge) when the pipeline is green AND comments are resolved. This is Fase 2 / BO #3 for issue #88. IMPORTANT PREREQUISITE FINDING: despite the issue narrative saying `_check_pr_ci` already exists, there is currently NO CI-check function anywhere in the codebase (grep-verified) — it must be created new. Keep flow/domain/ pure (no I/O): CI status and comment-resolution must be represented as data injected into the pure decision, exactly like the existing pr_head_sha parameter. All gh-facing I/O lives only in flow/adapters/github_transport.py (patchable) and orchestration in deployment/deployment.py.
steps: MODEL LAYER — flow/audit/state_comment.py: Extend ReviewerResult (frozen=True, slots=True dataclass) to represent the two additional pipeline signals so a single result object fully describes the gate. Add fields with backward-compatible defaults: `ci_green: bool | None = None` (None = unknown/not evaluated, e.g. legacy results or Jira with no CI) and `unresolved_comments: tuple[str, ...] = ()` (PR review threads still open). Update `is_auto_mergeable` so it returns True ONLY when approved AND len(comments)==0 AND ci_green is not False AND len(unresolved_comments)==0 (treat ci_green None as 'do not block' to preserve current behavior for legacy/Jira, mirroring how the SHA logic already tolerates missing info). Update set_reviewer_result() to accept and store the new fields (keep existing positional/kw signature working: add ci_green and unresolved_comments as trailing keyword params with defaults).

MODEL LAYER — render()/parse() round-trip: In render() extend the '### Resultado do Reviewer' section to include a `**Pipeline (CI):**` line (values e.g. 'verde' when ci_green is True, 'vermelho' when False, omit or 'n/d' when None) and, when unresolved_comments is non-empty, a `**Comentários pendentes:**` bulleted list. In _parse_block() add parsing for these so a rendered ReviewerResult round-trips (parse(render(sc)) preserves ci_green and unresolved_comments). Follow the exact existing parsing style used for '**SHA:**' and '**Pedidos de mudança:**'.

MODEL LAYER — render_pr_review_comment(): Extend the PR comment body so it always contains the COMPLETE information required by the acceptance criteria: the review status, reviewer, SHA, the CI/pipeline result, any unresolved PR comments, the list of change requests, AND an explicit link back to the responsible issue (issue_url is already a parameter). This is the 'complete info in both places' requirement for the PR side.

MODEL LAYER — issue side completeness: Ensure the issue also receives the COMPLETE result, not just a short reference. Add a new pure renderer (e.g. render_issue_review_result(reviewer_result, pr_number, pr_url)) in state_comment.py that produces the full review summary (what was done + link to PR + status + CI result + comments) suitable for posting/embedding on the issue. Keep the existing render_issue_pr_reference() for the short-reference callers that still want it, but the consolidated gate must ensure the full result reaches the issue (either via this renderer or by keeping the full ReviewerResult in the issue state comment via render()). Document in a docstring which function is authoritative.

DOMAIN LAYER — flow/executor/executor.py: The consolidated gate on the machine side is the REVIEW+REVIEWED branch that currently decides MERGE_PR vs NOTIFY_HUMAN. Add an injected parameter to decide() named `pr_ci_green: bool | None = None` (pure, no I/O — supplied by the deployment driving adapter, mirroring pr_head_sha). In the REVIEW+REVIEWED branch, before returning MERGE_PR: if the reviewer result would be auto-mergeable BUT pr_ci_green is False, do NOT merge — return NOTIFY_HUMAN (role TL) with a reason explaining the pipeline is red (pipeline vermelho) so a red CI never merges even if a stale reviewer result said approved. If pr_ci_green is None, preserve current behavior (do not block on unknown CI). Keep resolve_template and all other branches unchanged. Do NOT import any adapter/subprocess into the domain module.

ADAPTER LAYER — flow/adapters/github_transport.py: Add a new patchable transport function `get_pr_checks_status(owner_repo, pr_number) -> str` (or a small dict) that shells out to gh to read the PR CI rollup, e.g. `gh pr view <n> --repo <owner_repo> --json statusCheckRollup` and reduces it to a status string like 'green' | 'red' | 'pending' | 'none'. Follow the existing _run()/cast() and error-normalization conventions in this file (raise ProviderError family on failure). Add the corresponding thin wrapper in flow/adapters/github_client.py (e.g. get_pr_ci_status(project, pr_number)) following the pattern of get_pr_for_issue/merge_pull_request.

ORCHESTRATION — deployment/deployment.py: Implement/consolidate `_check_pr_ci` as the driving-adapter helper that calls github_client.get_pr_ci_status(...) and returns a bool|None (green->True, red/pending->False for gating merge but distinguish pending in the reason/log, none/error->None). In the REVIEW+REVIEWED code path in run() (the block near the existing pr_head_sha lookup) fetch the CI status and pass it to decide() via the new pr_ci_green argument. Ensure _execute_auto_merges / the MERGE_PR path calls _post_reviewer_result_on_pr so the COMPLETE result is posted to the PR and the issue is updated (this already happens for MERGE_PR and for the NOTIFY_HUMAN-with-reviewer-result path — verify BOTH branches post the full result to PR and issue, and extend _update_issue_with_pr_ref or use the new render_issue_review_result so the issue gets the COMPLETE info, not only the short reference). Do not merge when _check_pr_ci reports red.

PROMPT — flow/prompts/reviewer.md AND the _reviewer_fallback string in deployment/deployment.py: Update the one-shot reviewer instructions so the agent validates the WHOLE pipeline and PR comments before approving: add explicit steps to (a) check CI status with `gh pr checks {{pr_number}} --repo {{repo}}` and/or `gh pr view {{pr_number}} --repo {{repo}} --json statusCheckRollup` and treat a red/failing pipeline as NOT approved, (b) read and confirm PR review comments/threads are resolved, (c) only add crewflow:reviewed when CI is green AND comments are resolved AND there are zero change requests, and (d) always post the COMPLETE result (what was done + link + CI result + comments) to BOTH the PR and the issue. Keep the reviewer.md and the embedded fallback in deployment.py byte-for-byte consistent (there is an existing test asserting the fallback matches; keep them in sync). Preserve the {{placeholder}} contract — every placeholder used must be supplied by _reviewer_prompt().

TESTS — flow/tests/: Add tests covering the three required scenarios plus round-trips. (1) CI RED: in test_executor.py add a case where reviewer result is approved with zero comments but decide(..., pr_ci_green=False) returns NOTIFY_HUMAN TL (NOT MERGE_PR) with a reason mentioning the red pipeline; and pr_ci_green=True still yields MERGE_PR; pr_ci_green=None preserves MERGE_PR (legacy). (2) PENDING/UNRESOLVED COMMENTS: in test_audit_state_comment.py assert is_auto_mergeable is False when unresolved_comments is non-empty or ci_green is False, and True in the all-green case; assert render()/parse() round-trips ci_green and unresolved_comments. (3) ALL GREEN: assert the happy path (approved, no comments, ci_green True, no unresolved) => is_auto_mergeable True and decide(...) => MERGE_PR applying crewflow:done and removing crewflow:review+crewflow:reviewed. Add a deployment-level test in test_deployment_integration.py (or test_stage_entrypoints.py) that patches github_transport.get_pr_checks_status / github_client.get_pr_ci_status so that a red pipeline prevents the auto-merge and posts the complete result to the PR, using the existing mock.patch.object conventions (never real gh calls). Add a smoke assertion in test_prompts_loader.py TestRealTemplates that reviewer.md still renders with the required CI/comment instructions present.

Run the full verification (ruff, mypy, domain boundary test, full pytest with coverage) and fix anything until green. Confirm test_domain_boundary.py still passes (proves the CI signal was injected, not fetched inside the domain).
acceptance_criteria: Reviewer only approves/enables merge with green pipeline AND resolved comments: decide() returns NOTIFY_HUMAN TL (not MERGE_PR) when pr_ci_green is False, and ReviewerResult.is_auto_mergeable is False when ci_green is False or unresolved_comments is non-empty
The COMPLETE result (what was done + PR link + status + CI result + comments) is posted to BOTH the PR and the responsible issue in every path (approved and change-requested)
crewflow:reviewed is applied (enabling merge per BO #5) only when approved with green pipeline and resolved comments; the reviewer prompt adds it only under those conditions
New tests cover CI red, pending/unresolved comments, and all-green, and all pass
render()/parse() round-trip preserves the new ci_green and unresolved_comments fields
flow/tests/test_domain_boundary.py still passes (domain remains I/O-free; CI status is injected)
python3.12 -m ruff check flow/ is clean, mypy passes, and full pytest suite passes with coverage >=75%
verification: python3.12 -m pytest flow/tests/test_executor.py flow/tests/test_audit_state_comment.py flow/tests/test_deployment_integration.py flow/tests/test_stage_entrypoints.py flow/tests/test_prompts_loader.py -v
findings:
Implemented the consolidated single review gate for issue #88 (Fase 2 / BO #3). Changes: (1) flow/audit/state_comment.py — ReviewerResult gained ci_green:bool|None=None and unresolved_comments:tuple=() with backward-compatible defaults; is_auto_mergeable now also requires ci_green is not False AND no unresolved_comments (None does not block). render() adds '**Pipeline (CI):**' (verde/vermelho/n/d) and '**Comentários pendentes:**' lines; _parse_block() round-trips both. render_pr_review_comment() now always includes CI state + unresolved comments + issue link. Added render_issue_review_result() as the AUTHORITATIVE full-result renderer for the issue side. set_reviewer_result() accepts ci_green/unresolved_comments. (2) flow/executor/executor.py — decide() gained injected pr_ci_green:bool|None=None; in REVIEW+REVIEWED branch, an otherwise-auto-mergeable result with pr_ci_green is False returns NOTIFY_HUMAN TL (reason mentions pipeline vermelha) instead of MERGE_PR; None preserves legacy behavior. No I/O added — domain boundary test still passes. (3) flow/adapters/github_transport.py — new patchable get_pr_checks_status() reads gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup and reduces to green|red|pending|none. (4) flow/adapters/github_client.py — new get_pr_ci_status() wrapper (github is the parity REFERENCE so no jira mirror required; not part of IssueProvider protocol). (5) deployment/deployment.py — new _check_pr_ci() driving helper (green->True, red/pending->False, none/error->None, never raises); both run() and _run_stage() REVIEW+REVIEWED blocks fetch CI and pass pr_ci_green into decide(); _update_issue_with_pr_ref() now also posts the COMPLETE result to the issue via render_issue_review_result(); _reviewer_fallback updated in lock-step with reviewer.md. (6) flow/prompts/reviewer.md + fallback — reviewer now instructed to validate CI (gh pr checks / statusCheckRollup, red=not approved), confirm PR comments resolved, add crewflow:reviewed only when CI green AND comments resolved AND zero changes, and post the COMPLETE result to BOTH PR and issue. Placeholder contract preserved (no new placeholders). Tests added: executor CI red/green/None; audit ci_green/unresolved is_auto_mergeable + render/parse round-trips; render_issue_review_result + render_pr_review_comment CI/link; github transport get_pr_checks_status (green/red/error/pending/none) + client wrapper; deployment CI-gate (red blocks merge but posts full result; green merges). Verification (python3.12): ruff clean, mypy clean (47 files), test_domain_boundary.py green, full suite 522 passed + coverage 86.41% (>=75%). The single failure flow/tests/test_prompts_loader.py::TestRenderPromptFallback::test_template_corrompido_ilegivel_usa_fallback is pre-existing and root-only (chmod 0o000 bypassed by root); confirmed via git stash that it also fails on the FEAT-001 baseline. Docs (README + steering) intentionally deferred to FEAT-003.

Post-review polish (semantic review 2026-09-18-233336-review.md, APPROVED, 3 non-blocking issues): (1) FIXED — pending CI mislabeled as red. decide() gained an optional pr_ci_status:str|None tri-state label ('green'|'red'|'pending'|'none') injected ALONGSIDE the still-blocking pr_ci_green bool. When pr_ci_green is False the escalation reason now says 'pipeline (CI) ainda está pendente (em execução)' if pr_ci_status=='pending', else 'pipeline (CI) está vermelha'. Blocking is unchanged (both red and pending still return NOTIFY_HUMAN TL / block auto-merge); only the human-facing wording differs. _check_pr_ci() now returns tuple[bool|None, str|None] (gate, raw status); both run() and _run_stage() call sites unpack and pass pr_ci_status into decide(). Domain stays I/O-free (label is injected, never fetched); test_domain_boundary.py still passes. New tests: executor pending-blocks-but-labels-pendente, red-labels-vermelha, red-without-status-defaults-vermelha; deployment integration pending-blocks-merge-and-upserts-issue-result end-to-end. (2) JUSTIFIED + DOCUMENTED — no live re-check for unresolved_comments. Added an inline comment in executor.decide() (REVIEW+REVIEWED branch) explaining the asymmetry is intentional for this iteration: the reviewer is the authoritative source for comment resolution, a live thread re-fetch would widen scope (extra I/O + thread parsing) without the safety payoff CI has (CI can turn red AFTER review); the right fix if the reviewer under-reports is to strengthen the reviewer, not add domain I/O. (3) FIXED — full-result issue comment now idempotent (upsert-by-marker). Added ISSUE_REVIEW_RESULT_MARKER ('<!-- KIRO-FLOW-ISSUE-REVIEW -->') to state_comment.py; render_issue_review_result() now prefixes it. New github_client.upsert_issue_review_result() mirrors upsert_state_comment/upsert_pr_review_comment (0→create, 1→update in-place, N→update first + delete extras). _update_issue_with_pr_ref() now calls upsert_issue_review_result() instead of add_issue_comment(), so re-processing cannot stack duplicate full-result comments. New tests: TestUpsertIssueReviewResult (create/update/no-dup/idempotent-after-N/dedup-accumulated) and the deployment pending test asserts upsert (not append) is used and the marker is present. Verification (python3.12): ruff clean (flow/ and deployment/), mypy clean (47 files), test_domain_boundary.py green, full suite 530 passed + coverage 86.59% (>=75%); same single root-only prompt-loader failure as baseline. README/.kiro/steering already document 'CI vermelha/pendente' as both-blocking, consistent with the change — no doc edits needed.
